source: NCERT Class X, Democratic Politics II, Political Science Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. What are Political Parties?
points: A **political party** = a group of people who come together to **contest elections and hold power** in government; they agree on policies and programmes for the society's collective good.
Three components: **the leaders, the active members and the followers**.
Functions: **contest elections, put forward policies/programmes, make laws, form and run governments, act as opposition, shape public opinion, and provide access to welfare schemes**.

sections.heading: 2. Why Do We Need Parties? Party Systems
points: Parties are needed because they **gather diverse views, offer choices, and give accountable government**; without parties, every candidate would be independent and no policy or stability would be possible.

sub: **One-party system** — only one party allowed (e.g. China) — not democratic.
**Two-party system** — power usually alternates between two major parties (e.g. USA, UK).
**Multi-party system** — several parties compete; may form **alliances/fronts** (e.g. India — NDA, UPA). Suits a large, diverse society.

sections.heading: 3. National and State Parties
points: The **Election Commission** registers parties; **recognised** parties get a **symbol** and privileges.
**National party** — must secure a required vote share/seats in several states (e.g. **6% votes in 4 states + 4 Lok Sabha seats**, or 2% of Lok Sabha seats from 3 states).
**State party** — required vote share/seats within a state.
Examples: national parties (INC, BJP, BSP, CPI, CPI-M etc.); many strong **state/regional parties** reflect India's diversity.

sub: **Lack of internal democracy** — concentration of power in a few leaders.
**Dynastic succession** — top posts kept within a family.
**Money and muscle power** — especially at election time.
**No meaningful choice** — parties often not very different on fundamentals.
**Anti-defection law** — MLAs/MPs changing parties can be disqualified.
Candidates must **declare assets and criminal cases** (affidavit).
Election Commission's model code; demand for **state funding** and internal regulation.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Three components of a party: leaders, active members, followers.
National party = 6% votes in 4 states + 4 LS seats (one criterion).
Four challenges: lack of internal democracy, dynastic succession, money/muscle power, no real choice.
Anti-defection law disqualifies legislators who change parties.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: India has a **multi-party system** (leads to alliances like NDA/UPA).
The **anti-defection law** disqualifies legislators who **switch parties**.
The **Election Commission** recognises parties and allots symbols.
Candidates must file an **affidavit** declaring assets and criminal cases.
